rationale: Evidence from the baseline (entityR2A): all 60 trials went off track on all three tracks, with no finishes. Progress was only 0.12 to 0.16, max_error was about 0.063 (just past the 0.06 m off-track limit), and steering_oscillation was low (0.11 to 0.16). The failure is therefore a steady drift away from the line, not jitter. Line-loss events of 1 to 2 per run show the robot loses all sensors once its error passes roughly 0.035 m. The narrow sensor spread (±0.016 m, 0.012 m footprints) gives little warning and little steering authority before the line is lost. Changes: (1) Widen the sensor spread to x = -0.024, -0.012, 0, 0.012, 0.024 m and enlarge the footprint to 0.016 m, so the line stays visible at larger offsets and the signal responds earlier. (2) Raise kd from 0.15 to 0.3 to damp the drift-and-correct overshoot on the bends, since oscillation is low but the error is growing. (3) Lower base_speed from 1.6 to 1.5 to give the wider sensors and the damping time to act. This is the minimum speed that could plausibly still finish in 3 s. Keep kp 3.0, ki 0.05, weights antisymmetric, and line_loss last_direction. Expected result: fewer or no line-loss events, max_error below 0.06, and at least some completions on the oval and s-bend. The slalom may still be marginal. Hypotheses: H1, the drift is caused by weak sensor coverage at large offsets, so widening it cuts line-loss events. H2, the drift is partly due to too little damping, so kd 0.3 reduces max_error. H3, the speed is near the limit, so 1.5 keeps the robot on track. Next measurements wanted: completion and progress per track, max_error and where it peaks (bend type), line_loss_events and their timing, and completion_time to judge whether speed can be raised again.
